text:
noah: hey everyone, trying to run our docker-compose (postgres + redis) on Windows/WSL2. postgres fails to init with permission errors on the bind mount, and redis complains about loading from dump.rdb. i'm mounting `./data/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and `./data/redis:/data`. any WSL-specific tips?

jess: welcome! WSL2 has two common traps: using Windows paths from Docker Desktop vs using WSL filesystem. If your repo is on C:\Users and Docker Desktop is set to use the Windows backend, mounts can be slow or have weird perms. Put the repo inside the WSL filesystem (e.g., /home/<you>/repo) and run compose from there.

noah: ah i'm running from C:\Users\noah\repo via Powershell. moving into WSL sounds annoying. is there a quicker fix?

jess: short fix: enable WSL integration in Docker Desktop and open a WSL shell (wsl.exe) in the repo and run `docker-compose up` from inside WSL. Also set env `COMPOSE_CONVERT_WINDOWS_PATHS=1` if invoking compose from Windows powershell to help path conversion.

sam: +1. For the permission issue specifically, avoid host bind mounts for DB dirs on Windows. Use named volumes in compose or create the host dir in WSL and chown from a linux container: `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/data/postgres":/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data`.

noah: redis complaining about dump.rdb load errors too. could that be related?

jess: yes, if the file came from Windows with CRLF or got corrupted by the mount layer. Try removing the broken rdb and let redis create a fresh one: `rm -rf ./data/redis/dump.rdb` then `docker-compose up redis` to let it recreate. Also ensure file ownership: `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/data/redis":/data alpine chown -R 100:100 /data` (redis uid 100 in many images).

infra-bot: onboarding note: for Windows/WSL2 we recommend keeping project files in the WSL filesystem, enabling Docker WSL integration, using named volumes for DBs, and running `docker-compose down -v` when switching mounts. See docs: https://intranet.redwood.dev/dev-setup#wsl2

noah: moved the repo into WSL, removed the bad dump, used named volumes for postgres during testing, and postgres came up and migrations ran. thanks!

sam: nice. if you must keep repo on Windows drive, consider using docker volumes and rsync-based sync tools for dev files rather than direct bind mounts.

noah: good to know. appreciate the help :)
